If you want to flush your firewall rules, you'll need to run that command yourself on the target machine (as root):

```bash
sudo iptables -F && sudo iptables -X && sudo iptables -P INPUT ACCEPT && sudo iptables -P FORWARD ACCEPT
```

⚠️ A quick heads-up before you run it: this will **wipe all firewall rules, delete custom chains, and set INPUT/FORWARD policies to ACCEPT** — effectively leaving the host with no firewall protection. If you're on a remote machine, make sure that's intended (it's generally safe for connectivity since you're opening things up, but it does expose all listening services). You may also want to set `OUTPUT ACCEPT` and flush the `nat`/`mangle` tables explicitly if that's your goal:

```bash
sudo iptables -P OUTPUT ACCEPT
sudo iptables -t nat -F && sudo iptables -t nat -X
sudo iptables -t mangle -F && sudo iptables -t mangle -X
```
